title: Introduce coroutine-based continuous-batcher and compact KV warmup path
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Replace the legacy fiber/threadpool-based continuous batching path with a coroutine-first implementation and introduce a compact KV warmup path to reduce cold-start footprint and tail latency.
Scope: 1) Migrate core continuous-batcher state machine to C++20 coroutines (stackless) for lower overhead and clearer control flow; 2) Add a minimal 'compact warmup' path for KV cache priming that trades completeness for speed on cold starts (sampled priming + lazy rehydrate); 3) Simplify the scheduler interface by removing the separate fiber pool adapter and folding admission decisions into the coroutine dispatcher; 4) Trim a small set of runtime dependencies that block modern compiler flags (remove Boost.Future usage, vendor minimal helper types).
Motivation: Current batcher relies on a custom fiber pool and several Boost utilities causing significant allocation churn and complexity whenever a model swap or node restart occurs. Cold KV priming currently fetches many redundant shards, causing long p99 startup times for small-sequence workloads.
Success metrics:
- p50 token latency for 32-token requests: <= current - 15% (target)
- p99 end-to-end latency for small seq loads: -25% at 95th percentile
- KV warmup memory spike reduced by 40% on node start
- CI safety: zero regressions in existing unit/integration tests
Approach/Design Notes:
- Coroutines chosen for clearer async flow and reduced heap allocations; will use std::coroutine_handle-based dispatcher with a single event loop per worker for fairness.
- Compact KV warmup will run as a prioritized background coroutine that primes hot keys (top-N) using a lightweight sampler and defers full shard reconciliation.
- Scheduler simplification removes the legacy fiber adapter and maps admission tokens to coroutine tasks with tight backpressure signals.
Tradeoffs/Risks:
- Coroutines require C++20 toolchain; will gate with feature flag and maintain legacy path for canary rollouts.
- Stackless coroutines limit arbitrary stack usage; some existing callsites need rework (notably legacy IO helpers) which required small refactors.
- Debugging async stack traces is harder; we add richer trace IDs in telemetry and tie to tracing hooks in the console.
Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests converted to coroutine-friendly fixtures.
- Synthetic microbench harness updated to replay historical traffic traces (last 7 days) to validate latency/cost.
- Nightly canary on 10% of Dedicated capacity followed by 50% and full rollout if no infra alerts for 48h.
Observability:
- New dashboard: batcher/coroutine-disp/latency and batcher/kv/compact-warmup/coverage.
- Added labels on spans to identify coroutine task IDs and warmup sampling decisions.
Rollout Plan:
1) Internal branch + CI (done)
2) Feature-flagged canary on non-customer Dedicated pool (10%)
3) Canary on low-traffic customer tier (5 customers)
4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with automated rollback on SLO breach.
Rollback Strategy: Re-enable legacy fiber path via runtime flag and drain tasks; warmup behavior will fall back to full reconcile.

comments: 2026-02-11 - Sofia Martinez: Spike concluded. Coroutine spike reduced per-request allocations by ~18% in microbench for small payloads. Identified three callsites relying on stackful behavior; scheduled small refactors.

2026-02-20 - Daniel Kim: Converted admission controller to dispatcher shim. Initial CI failures due to legacy io::buffer helpers — added thin adapter layer to maintain behavior while we migrate callsites.
2026-02-28 - PR #4821 opened. Early perf run shows p99 improvement of ~12% at low load, CI flaky on macOS toolchain due to coroutine ABI differences. Filed infra ticket to standardize compiler flags.
2026-03-03 - Security review: no sensitive surface changes; KV warmup sampling introduces probabilistic reads but still honors existing access controls. Marked security_review_required=false.
2026-03-07 - QA: Integration tests passed for model-swap scenarios; observed occasional task starvation under synthetic adversarial load. Added fairness yield in dispatcher after 256 executed steps.

2026-03-10 - Daniel Kim: Canary run on internal pool (10%). Metrics: p50 latency -13%, p99 -18%, KV mem spike -37%. Two small regressions traced to higher CPU on tight loops; optimizing allocator usage next.

2026-03-12 - Design review (pm/dev): Agreed to keep legacy path behind flag for 30 days. Action: add alert thresholds and a dashboard annotation for rollback windows. Next: complete PR cleanup, address CI cross-compile failures, and schedule customer canary.
